html:
Moldavia became an independent principality around 1359, when Bogdan, a Romanian noble from Maramureș, crossed the Carpathians, drove out the deputies of the king of Hungary and made himself its ruler.

Hungary had set up a march there against the Tatars of the Golden Horde. Bogdan's lands, with their early capitals at Baia, Siret and Suceava, grew to reach the Dniester and the Black Sea. Moldavia reached its height under Stephen the Great, then became a tributary of the Ottoman Empire in the 1500s while keeping its own princes. Its eastern half, Bessarabia, went to Russia in 1812 and is today's Moldova. The western half joined Wallachia in 1859 to form Romania.
sum: Moldavia became an independent principality around 1359, when Bogdan, a Romanian noble from Maramureș, crossed the Carpathians, drove out the deputies of the king of Hungary and made himself its ruler.
